answer: The wander test I would run is Dental treatment history with practice records: treatments recorded at one dental practice over years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that treatments recorded at one dental practice over years — so privacy survives, and the orchard is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the relic of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
